extracted.intended_audience: readers/contributors of the n-Category Café who want to post material to the nLab wiki (mathematicians, physicists, philosophers comfortable with LaTeX/Markdown)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for copying, formatting, and converting blog comments or LaTeX material so they can be posted and edited on the nLab Instiki wiki (including tool recommendations and limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy-and-paste the source, not the rendered output
rubrics_metrics.description: You are supposed to copy-and-paste the source code of a blog comment into the nLab, not to try to copy and paste the output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The markdown+itex source makes it easier for others to edit the entry. While you can paste XHTML+MathML directly, using the source (markdown+itex) is preferred so Lab editors can modify content. If quoting others' comments, getting their source is often impossible for ordinary users (admins may recover it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Save a local copy of your comment before posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Save a copy of your comment before you submit it to the Cafe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should save their source while composing (some people do this anyway to avoid losing text). If you later decide to move the content to the nLab and you didn't save the source, it's not easy to recover it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 'Markdown with itex to MathML' filter
rubrics_metrics.description: The How to get started page refers to using the Markdown with itex to MathML filter by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This filter is the recommended way to produce MathML from itex for the nLab. Users expect the filter to be selected when posting; currently preferences may not be saved automatically, so selecting it manually or requesting a default-setting is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the main HowTo short and 'good enough'
rubrics_metrics.description: The HowTo page should be short so people actually read it and get the impression that contributing is easy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a quick working definition that produces good results to first approximation. Detailed or tricky issues should be put on supplementary pages branched off from the main HowTo so the primary page remains concise and approachable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide two separate procedures: own posts vs external material
rubrics_metrics.description: Have different instructions for (a) forwarding your own blog post to the Lab and (b) posting material you find elsewhere on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting other people's web material is trickier because converters are often one-way. Best practical approach: copy what you see and manually hack it back into markdown+itex, or ask an admin to retrieve the original source and email it to you. The HowTo should explicitly distinguish the two cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t rely on preamble-defined macros (Instiki limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use all plain standard LaTeX commands, but not predefined macros etc; macros don't work on Instiki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your document uses definitions like \def\g{\mathfrak{g}} in the preamble, these won't be available on the nLab. Workarounds include performing a careful search-and-replace to expand macros back to their full forms before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle macro-heavy LaTeX by expansion or conversion tools
rubrics_metrics.description: For material heavy in macros, the quickest method might be to set up emacs macros or write a parser to replace macros, or use conversion tools (tex4ht, PHPLaTeX, GELLMU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options and tradeoffs: manual expansion (emacs macros) is simple for many cases; writing a parser can automate repetitive replacements; using tools like tex4ht, PHPLaTeX or GELLMU can convert whole documents but differ in speed, portability and setup complexity (see individual-tool guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer tex4ht when fidelity to full LaTeX is required
rubrics_metrics.description: The easiest way to convert full LaTeX, including macros and arbitrary packages, to XHTML+MathML is to use tex4ht.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tex4ht uses a full LaTeX backend (slower) and typically needs command-line tweaking to get best results, so it's not ideal for automated translation but gives the best fidelity for difficult LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider GELLMU for semantic conversion, but note implementation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: GELLMU is a markup language similar to LaTeX that strips non-semantic constructs and is easier to convert to other semantic languages; it supports \newcommand but not packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GELLMU can make web conversion cleaner, but it's implemented in Emacs Lisp which makes web deployment harder; it's a tradeoff between semantic clarity and ease-of-deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use token-expansion approaches (PHPLaTeX) to preserve macro expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: PHPLaTeX was developed to convert subsets of LaTeX (xymatrix, tikz) to XHTML+MathML+SVG using token expansion so macro expansion behaves properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHPLaTeX is slower than itex but preserves macro semantics via token expansion rather than brittle pattern-matching. It can be a good middle ground when macro expansion is required but a full tex4ht pipeline is undesirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pasting raw XHTML+MathML as primary authoring mode
rubrics_metrics.description: You can paste XHTML+MathML directly into the nLab, but markdown+itex syntax makes it easier for others to edit the entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do paste XHTML+MathML, be aware it may make later edits harder; authors are encouraged to supply markdown+itex when possible so the community can collaboratively improve the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design error pages as flat HTML with minimal dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Error pages ought to be as simple as possible — in particular, flat HTML files — so that they have as few dependencies as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since error pages may be shown when site components fail, keep them raw HTML and lightweight. They should provide the information users expect (for instance, a link to 'Latest Changes' when 'Recently Revised' is disabled) rather than complex dynamic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: When converting diagrams (xymatrix, tikz), prefer direct SVG output or dedicated converters
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting xymatrix diagrams to SVG was a principal motivation; tikz->SVG via tex4ht can be poor, so consider dedicated converters or token-expansion approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because MathML+SVG interactions can be tricky, producing native SVG that integrates well with the MathML output often gives better results; this may require bespoke parsers or converters (lex/yacc-style tools) rather than general-purpose converters.

rubrics_metrics.name: List and use available supporting plugins/tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The blog references several tools/plugins used to produce MathML and support the blog-to-lab workflow (itex2MML, itexToMML, MTValidate, SVGfix, NumericEntities, PHPLaTeX, tex4ht, GELLMU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and maintainers should be aware of these components and their roles. Where possible, porting or packaging converters as plugins (e.g., for MovableType, Melody) can help broader adoption; check MT templates and plugin configuration for correct integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the HowTo produce 'good results to first approximation' for lab elves
rubrics_metrics.description: The HowTo should give a quick working definition that produces good results to first approximation so that the lab elves can pick up and polish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for instructions that enable easy initial contributions; community editors can later refine formatting, macros, and cross-linking. Avoid overloading the newcomer-facing page with implementation complexity.
